name: manual_32aea4
claim: git restore --staged --worktree . discards ALL unrelated staged and unstaged changes in the working tree, not just the undone cherry-pick's files -- it is a destructive broad-reset disguised as cleanup. Before running it, require a clean git status --short (verifying nothing unrelated is dirty), or scope the restore to only the specific paths the undone commit touched (git restore --staged --worktree -- <path>...). The git update-ref refs/heads/<name> <sha> guidance itself remains correct and unaffected.

decisions.notes: CodeRabbit PR #334 review 4871403999: the git restore --staged --worktree . guidance in lesson_e276758511e6 is unsafe as written -- it discards unrelated tracked changes repo-wide, not just the undone cherry-pick. Corrected via proper supersession (original left untouched, per lesson_9940e1aa6fc4's own doctrine) rather than editing the graduated record or the episodic log entry in place.
